function.arguments: {"index": 4, "status": "acted", "resolution": "The `converted` column is defined as 1 if the order completed checkout, which occurs at the time of purchase, not at final settlement. Refunded orders are still counted as 'converted' in the data (e.g., order ORD00020 has `converted=1` and `status=refunded`). Therefore, to compute the conversion rate correctly, we must include all orders in the group — including refunded ones — because the question is about the fraction of customers who converted (i.e., checked out), not the fraction of successful final transactions. Excluding refunded orders would undercount both the numerator and denominator, biasing the rate downward. The analysis was corrected to include all orders in the NEW + PAID SEARCH group, regardless of status."}
